A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 14-page versions of R2IF, with matching main sections and Appendices A–G. Full-text comparison and rendered-page checks support reliable comparison of the text, equations, figures and tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original BFCL and ACEBench experiments, component ablations, and appendix studies covering multi-turn interaction, sampling robustness, computational overhead and human evaluation.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the benchmark evaluations and the eight-evaluator human study in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The GRPO training procedure, binary/CER/SMV reward components, student evaluator and SFT warm-start are unchanged. The appendix reward variant and prompts are also retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ToolACE training data and BFCL/ACEBench task coverage. The appendix multi-turn, student-evaluator and human-evaluation scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments: Raw, SFT, Binary Reward and ToolRL remain, alongside the same component ablations and Appendix C's R2IF-toolrl comparison.

E3.justification: The 2,500-sample training set, backbones, accuracy and ACE metrics, training configurations and appendix evaluation procedures are unchanged. The Table 5 numerical correction is not accompanied by a reported setting change.

E4.justification: The existing component-ablation evidence is locally revised through Table 5's corrected Qwen2.5-7B full-model reference. On ACEBench Single Turn, R2IF now exceeds all three ablated variants, whereas v1's table placed it below them. Ablation variants and other supplementary analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix B retains the same CER sampling and ranking-stability reporting. Appendix E retains the same significance threshold and Cronbach's alpha reporting; no run-count or uncertainty-reporting changes appear.

E6.justification: In Table 5, Qwen2.5-7B R2IF's ACEBench Atom, Single Turn and Irrelevant scores change from 73.70/51.00/94.00 to 78.00/57.50/96.00. These now match Table 3 in both versions; the overall score remains 77.17. All other results are unchanged, supporting a reporting correction rather than a demonstrated performance gain.

T1.justification: The function-calling formalization, GRPO objective, reward definitions and ACE formula are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about reasoning–decision alignment, accuracy, interpretability and generalization. The corrected table entries do not change those claims.

C2.justification: The explanations of component effects, scaling and generalization, together with the limitations and appendix interpretations, are unchanged. The prose discussing Table 5 is not revised.

D1.justification: Hardware, frameworks, data preparation, student-evaluator details, training hyperparameters in Tables 14–15 and prompts in Figures 4–5 are unchanged. No technical or code/data access information is added.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion and positioning relative to prior function-calling and reasoning-supervision methods are identical.

P1.justification: The author email changes from ling.shi@ntu.edu.cn to ling.shi@ntu.edu.sg, and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. The narrative, headings and document structure are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures, tables, captions, styling and placement are retained. Table 5 changes only numerical entries within its existing display; the author-contact and version-stamp edits do not reorganize the layout.

improvement.justification: v1 reports conflicting Qwen2.5-7B ACEBench subscores in Tables 3 and 5. v2 makes Table 5 agree with Table 3 and the unchanged 77.17 overall score, resolving an internal inconsistency and improving the basis for interpreting the ablations. This is a limited reporting improvement; the scientific scope and study designs remain unchanged.
